organizations.name: Miami Waterkeeper
organizations.overview: Miami Waterkeeper (formerly Biscayne Bay Waterkeeper) is a Miami-based nonprofit that has worked since 2010 to protect Biscayne Bay and Miami-Dade's waterways through science, community engagement, and legal advocacy.

accomplishments.text: Won legal standing to join a federal Clean Water Act lawsuit against Miami-Dade County over water and sewer infrastructure the county allegedly failed to repair for as much as 50 years.

plannedActivities.text: Running a 'Stop Septic Pollution' campaign for Miami-Dade County. Both Miami Shores and El Portal, the two villages bordering this address, have active septic-to-sewer conversion projects (Miami Shores' $3M Shores Estates project started June 2025; El Portal's $20.3M plan covers ~840 septic properties) — though this exact property's own septic vs. sewer status isn't confirmed.
Opposing Miami-Dade's $12.6 billion water and sewer repair plan, arguing it fails to account for sea-level rise and storm surge risk.
